newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean activists vow to block nuke waste move.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean activists vow to block nuke waste move.

text.p: South Korean activists said on Wednesday that they would forcibly block the planned transfers of nuclear waste from Taiwan to North Korea.

"If Taiwan and North Korea refuse to abandon the contract, we have no choice but to forcibly block the North Korean ships from shipping the nuclear waste," Jang Won, leader of the environmental organisation Green Korea, told reporters.
He gave no details, but said their plans would require a special vessel such as the Rainbow Warrior used by militant environmental group Greenpeace.

Jang was expelled from Taiwan on January 30 with six other South Korean activists after protesting outside the state-run Taiwan Power Co, which signed a deal on January 11 to send 60,000 barrels of nuclear waste to North Korea over a two-year span.
Under the contract, Taipower has the option to a total of up to 200,000 barrels of nuclear waste to North Korea.
Tensions between Taiwan and South Korea increased when Taipei flatly rejected Seoul's request to drop the deal.
